races.title: State House, District 56
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Allen Buansi
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina House for District 56 since June 2022, appointed to replace Verla Insko. Civil rights lawyer and former assistant city attorney. Served on the Chapel Hill Town Council from 2017 to 2021. Graduated from Dartmouth College (2009) and UNC School of Law (2015).

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among his 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations on Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from Buansi on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration enforcement or H-1B, policing and public safety, or gun policy. His bills are not itemized in the pages we could read. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys. His campaign site appears to date from his 2022 run, so it may not reflect his current positions. His stance on school choice and vouchers is not documented in what we reviewed.

local.label: Roots 90: He was born in Evanston, Illinois, moved to North Carolina at age ten, and says he grew up in Chapel Hill and attended its public schools.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Member of the NC House since 2022; Chapel Hill Town Council member 2017-2021; civil rights lawyer and assistant city attorney; served on the state Local Government Retirement System Board of Trustees 2018-2021.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service (state House since 2022) plus local elected office and a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets. The board seats were not counted.
qual.label: He has prior legislative service (state House since 2022) plus local elected office and a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets. The board seats were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says all women should have the right to choose and to have access to safe abortions, and that he would codify abortion access as it was before Roe and Casey were overturned.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he would pay school personnel a fair and competitive wage, noting North Carolina ranks in the bottom half of states in teacher pay. It says nothing about vouchers, charters or school choice, and stresses fully funding public schools.

cands.name: Matthew P. Clements
cands.bio: Information technology professional and Libertarian. Ran for the NC House in District 56 in 2018 and 2026, and for Carrboro Town Council in 2019. Has held no elected office, according to the sources found.
cands.gaps: We found no information on where he was born or raised or when he moved to North Carolina. His employers and specific job history are not documented, so his management experience can't be checked. He has held no voting office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. His 2026 survey does not take a position on data centers, homestead property taxes, land purchases by investors or foreign buyers, guns, abortion, school choice, teacher pay, police funding or immigration enforcement. He wrote that Orange County is restricted by state laws overriding local zoning, but he did not state a position on development itself. He listed no endorsements. No news coverage or controversies were found.
